response.query: What principled mapping converts multi‑tranche liabilities (TLAC, senior, subordinated, secured repo) and off‑balance exposures into an effective single-claim Merton inversion?
response.answer: The Merton model converts multi-tranche liabilities and off-balance exposures into an effective single-claim inversion by treating them as a single entity's equity. This model uses the firm's asset value to estimate default probability. It simplifies complex financial structures into a single risk metric.

results.title: How to Report Subordinated Debt on a Balance Sheet
results.content: # How to Report Subordinated Debt on a Balance Sheet. In these situations, subordinated debt is a financing option your firm may want to use to raise needed capital when other sources aren't forthcoming. ## Subordinated Debt Definition. The debts the firm owes are ranked, with the highest priority or senior debt being paid first. Lower priority debt obligations are subordinate to the senior debt because they are paid only after senior debts are cleared in the event the business is liquidated. Each debt is subordinate to all other debts with a higher priority. For example, a secured bank loan is senior debt and bonds are subordinate to it. ## Reporting Subordinated Debt. As borrowed money, subordinated debt goes in the liabilities section. Typically, senior debt is entered on the balance sheet next. Subordinated debt is listed last in the liabilities section in descending order of priority. When a business takes out a loan or sells bonds that are subordinated debt, the cash or property acquired with the borrowed funds is added capital and goes in the assets section. How to Determine a Company's Total Debt on a Balance Sheet. How to Determine a Company's Total Debt on a Balance Sheet. Interest on subordinated debt must be paid on a regular schedule. As an expense, subordinated debt interest is reported on a firm's income statement and not on the balance sheet. Subordinated debt interest is a tax-deductible expense on the income statement. Subordinated debt has the advantage that ownership's share of the business isn't diluted by added equity. The money raised can be used for any purpose allowed by the terms of the borrowing agreement, but typically firms use subordinated debt to finance growth. For example, a retail business might use subordinated debt to add new store locations. Banks holding senior debt with the business may look favorably on subordinated debt because it increases the total assets on the balance sheet available to pay off debt in the event the firm fails. On the downside, subordinated debt carries more risk for lenders and so tends to have high interest rates.
